requestSummary: Create a complete, shareable Markdown overview explaining what Project Orchestrator is, what it is for, how to use it, and why it is valuable.
confirmedRequirements: Create docs/PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md as a standalone, shareable document without replacing the generated canonical project guide.
Address mixed leadership and engineering readers by leading with value and following with technical and operational detail.
Organize the document as an executive summary plus a complete technical guide.
Explain purpose, problems solved, differentiated value, architecture, capabilities, workflows, installation, usage, governance, validation, limitations, pilot adoption, and terminology.
Ground every claim and command in current repository evidence and retain the internal-only, unsigned-candidate release boundary.
projectFacts: Project Orchestrator version 1.1.1 and framework version 9.0.0 provide a registry-free Node.js runtime and 44 governed skills.
The runtime supports Node.js 22, 24, and 26 and uses no application package dependencies.
It can create a governed baseline, adopt an existing local repository, clone and adopt a GitHub repository, and update an installed standalone project while preserving project-owned content.

Core controls include bounded clarification, stack-aware installation, overlap detection, dry-run planning, explicit risk acceptance, transactional writes, rollback and recovery, policy decisions, schemas, event-sourced state, and machine-readable reports.
Agent Builder creates and validates least-privilege local agent definitions and publication handoff plans without deploying or publishing external resources.

The current evidence reports 124 passing tests, zero failures, one platform-specific skip, 44 audited skills, 219 security-scanned files, and 158 checksum-covered candidate files; release remains blocked.
assumptions: The user's unavailable response selects the recommended new-document, mixed-audience, and executive-summary-plus-technical-guide defaults.

The document may recommend a bounded pilot but must not imply public distribution or production readiness.
